title: A first collaboration conversation with FamilieSCN2A Foundation

sentences.text: At KCNQ2 Cure Alliance, we support KCNQ2 families, while FamilieSCN2A Foundation supports families with SCN2A-related disorders.
Both genes help nerve cells fire, and published research describes variants that make their proteins do too much.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms between our disorders, but this connection has confidence 0.48, below 0.5—not proof that families have the same needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Citizen Health collects medical-record information about life with KCNQ2-related disorders, and the COMBINEDBrain Biorepository holds family-donated samples for KCNQ2 research.
The Registry and Natural History of Epilepsy-Dyskinesia Syndromes also includes KCNQ2 in its study criteria.
We could begin by comparing these resources and discussing which approaches might be useful together, without assuming access or compatibility.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: The proposed biological bridge is loss of function—reduced protein activity—but the broad KCNQ2 connection is contested because other variants have different effects; we should read both sides in the evidence panel.
Please help us check whether poor gross motor coordination, facial erythema and myokymia occur in SCN2A-related disorders, rather than treating missing records as absence.
Before joining forces, we should also identify additional KCNQ2 organizations and research resources, and check individual variant effects.
Send FamilieSCN2A Foundation one focused inquiry asking whether the Dragonfly patient registry could include KCNQ2-related disorders and what would need checking first.
What patient organizations, registries, trials and research groups exist for KCNQ2-related disorders beyond those verified here?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired—that is, less able to perform their chemical work—or loss of function?
I am reaching out on behalf of KCNQ2 Cure Alliance to explore a modest collaboration.
Could we discuss whether the Dragonfly patient registry could include KCNQ2-related disorders?
We would welcome your guidance on feasibility and the differences we should check first.
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of KCNQ2 Cure Alliance
